speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin the assessment, could you please tell me how many weeks pregnant you are and when the vaginal bleeding and abdominal pain started?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old woman, gravida 2, para 1, at 38 weeks' gestation. The patient reports experiencing vaginal bleeding for the past hour accompanied by severe abdominal pain. She mentions that she felt contractions before the onset of the bleeding, but the contractions ceased once the bleeding began. Her first childbirth was a cesarean section due to nonreassuring fetal heart rate.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you. Is the abdominal pain continuous and severe, and have you noticed any vaginal discharge or fluid leakage?

REQUEST TEST: Fetal_Heart_Rate_Monitoring

speaker: Doctor
text: The fetal heart rate shows recurrent variable decelerations, which is concerning. Do you feel any tearing sensation or a "pop" in your abdomen, and is the pain localized to the site of your previous cesarean scar?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Vaginal bleeding. I also have Severe abdominal pain, History of contractions that stopped, Previous cesarean delivery.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The combination of vaginal bleeding, severe pain, cessation of contractions, and a prior cesarean section is highly suggestive of uterine rupture. I will request an immediate ultrasound to confirm the integrity of the uterus and assess fetal status.

REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_Ultrasound

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Suggestive of a disruption in the uterine wall continuity adjacent to the scar from the previous cesarean section, with associated hemoperitoneum.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The ultrasound confirms a disruption in the uterine wall and internal bleeding, which is consistent with uterine rupture given your history and symptoms. This is a life-threatening emergency requiring immediate surgical intervention.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Uterine Rupture
